title: The cascara experiment
summary: Cherry husk, steeped like tea. Six weeks of bench notes, and the two things we got wrong first.
body:
Cascara is the dried skin of the coffee cherry — the part a washing station usually throws away. Our Bolivian producer kept a sack back for us, and we spent six weeks working out what to do with it.

The first mistake was treating it as coffee. It is not coffee; it is closer to a rooibos with a hibiscus edge, and it wants tea water and tea time — 90 degrees, four minutes, no pressure anywhere near it.

The second mistake was the ratio. We started at coffee strength and it was medicinal. 8 g to 300 g is the number we landed on, and it is the number on the bag.

This post used to live at a different address, which is why there is a redirect pointing here. The [journal index](/blog/) has the rest of the bench notes.
